title: Composable Admin Utility SDK and Stepwise Remediation Sequencer
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight, composable Admin Utility SDK and runtime sequencer that converts declarative support procedures into typed, idempotent tasks that can be executed manually or by automation. The goal is to enable first-line support and automated responders to run multi-step remediation flows with strong telemetry, RBAC, and safety checks without shipping bespoke scripts.

Motivation: We currently have many disparate admin scripts and ad-hoc runbooks. Developers and oncall spend time re-authoring basic fixes for different contexts. This work aims to standardize: (1) a small SDK for authors to declare steps (inputs, outputs, preconditions, rollback), (2) a sequencer that interprets those steps into an executable task graph with checkpoints, dry-run, and replay, and (3) integrations for telemetry, audit logging, and GitHub/Console linking so actions are observable and auditable.

Scope:
- SDK: Type definitions (TypeScript + Python stubs), helpers for idempotency tokens, safe side-effect wrappers, RBAC checks, and metrics hooks.
- Sequencer: Deterministic step runner with concurrency controls, retry semantics, and checkpoint snapshots. Supports interactive mode (human-in-the-loop confirmations) and headless mode for automation.
- Safety: Precondition gating (feature flags, canary percentage), permission-scope enforcement, simulated dry-run, and automatic rollback support for reversible steps.
- Observability: Emit structured events to the Console telemetry ingestion (trace id, step id, latency, result), surface per-step costs in the cost dashboard, and link back to originating GitHub PR or Confluence procedure.
- UX hooks: CLI shim for quick invocation, and a Console widget to surface sequencer state and allow safe escalation to automation.

Non-goals: End-to-end incident automation (this ticket focuses on the framework; incident-specific recipes live in separate tickets). No new infra clusters.

Deliverables:
1) admin-sdk v0.1 (TS + py stubs) published to internal package registry
2) sequencer service (containerized) with REST API and websocket streaming for interactive sessions
3) CLI -> Console integration and a sample canonical remediation (DB connection rotation) with telemetry dashboard
4) Security review notes and RBAC matrix

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will favor strict typing in the SDK to reduce ambiguous step inputs; this increases initial authoring friction but reduces runtime failures.
- Sequencer will persist checkpoints to existing ops-state store (avoid building new DB). We will implement optimistic concurrency and allow step-scoped locking for external resources.
- To keep latency low for common fixes, the sequencer will support local mode (run steps in the caller process) vs remote mode (sequencer service). Local mode is for quick manual fixes and will run with constrained permissions.

Integration links:
- Design intent doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Composable+Admin+SDK+RFC
- Telemetry dashboard (proto): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ops-sdk-v0.1
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/542

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK package published and used by 2 internal recipes
- Sequencer can run the sample DB rotation flow end-to-end in both dry-run and live modes
- Structured telemetry emitted for each step and visible in Console traces
- Security review completed and RBAC enforced for all dangerous actions

Risks:
- Authoring errors could still cause unsafe remediation; mitigated by dry-run + canary gating.
- Persisted checkpoint model could conflict with long-running external ops; mitigated by leases and ttl-based cleanup.

Next milestones:
- 2026-02-20: SDK alpha published + basic examples
- 2026-02-28: Sequencer PoC (local mode) with CLI shim
- 2026-03-12: Remote sequencer + telemetry integration
- 2026-03-20: Security review and internal dogfood
